answer: Agents must produce cryptographic proofs that their model weights differ from all registered agents by a minimum Hamming distance, verified via zero-knowledge proofs over commitment trees. An attacker creating N sybils must train N genuinely distinct models (cost: N × training compute) rather than copying weights. The protocol samples random layers per epoch; proofs reveal only distance metrics, not weights. At the voyage's dawn, each new vertex in the agent graph pays this differentiation tax, making sybil farms economically irrational unless each identity provides unique cognitive value.
